A_target.statement:
Let $S$ be a set of [[Definition:Clause (Logic)|clauses]].
If the empty clause is derivable from $S$ by [[Definition:Resolution Rule|resolution]], then $S$ is [[Definition:Unsatisfiable|unsatisfiable]].

B_source.statement: To show that a proof system is sound, show that each inference rule preserves truth under every valuation, and induct over derivations.

derived.truth preservation: every derived clause holds under any valuation satisfying S

object_map.reformulation: Apply the rule-by-rule soundness plan to the resolution calculus, whose only rule is resolution.

validity_conditions: The empty clause is satisfied by no valuation, which gives the contradiction.
Completeness of resolution for refutation is a separate, harder result.
proof_plan: Suppose a valuation $v$ satisfies every clause of $S$.

From $C \lor p$ and $D \lor \neg p$, resolution infers $C \lor D$.
If $\map v p = 1$ then $v \models D$, and otherwise $v \models C$; in either case $v \models C \lor D$.
By induction on the length of the derivation, $v$ satisfies every derived clause.
